opex.name: Operations & maintenance
opex.note: Running and repairing power plants, wind and solar fleets, and the grid day to day.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of power plants, transmission lines and renewable projects over their long lives — a non-cash charge that grows with NextEra's huge build-out.

opex.name: Taxes other than income taxes
opex.note: Mostly property taxes on power plants and networks, plus franchise and payroll-type taxes.

opex.name: Merger-related expenses
opex.note: Costs of the pending combination with Dominion Energy, approved by both companies' shareholders in September 2026.

opex.name: Gains on disposal of assets, net
opex.note: A net credit: NextEra sold businesses/assets for $44M more than their book value, which reduces expenses here.

follow100Note: The 'other income' row is unusually large because it includes $3.0B of mark-to-market hedge gains (about $37 per $100 of revenue) — paper gains that NextEra itself excludes from its adjusted earnings.
footerNote: Adaptation for a utility: fuel and purchased power is treated as the cost of revenue; the remaining operating lines mirror NextEra's income statement, including a $44M net gain on asset disposals shown as a negative expense. Net income is the $4,775M attributable to NextEra: consolidated net income was $4,367M, and outside partners in NextEra's projects absorbed $408M of losses, which is added back below the line here (the equityM line). Segment revenues are as reported by segment and sum to consolidated revenue.
oneTimers: $3,005M of pre-tax mark-to-market gains on non-qualifying hedges (derivatives that don't get hedge accounting) flowed through earnings — mostly in Corporate & Other. NextEra excludes them from adjusted earnings, which is why adjusted EPS is $1.24, not $2.28.
$19M of merger-related expenses for the pending Dominion Energy combination, which both companies' shareholders approved in September 2026.
A $50M unrealized loss on equity securities held in the nuclear decommissioning funds.
otherDetail: Dominated by $3,005M of mark-to-market gains on non-qualifying hedges, plus $293M of equity-method earnings, $65M of construction allowance and $44M of gains on investment disposals, partly offset by interest expense and a $50M mark-down on nuclear decommissioning fund investments. A further $408M is the share of project losses absorbed by outside partners, which lifts profit attributable to NextEra above consolidated net income.

segments.name: Florida Power & Light (FPL)
segments.note: America's largest electric utility — regulated power for Florida at prices set by regulators. Revenue up 3%; FPL earned $1,620M as regulatory capital employed grew about 9% on roughly $2.4B of quarterly capital spending.

segments.name: NextEra Energy Resources
segments.note: The competitive energy arm — the world's largest wind and solar generator, plus nuclear, gas, storage and transmission. Revenue down 2%, but attributable profit rose to $1,491M; it added 3.7 GW to a backlog now near 36.7 GW.

segments.name: Corporate & other
segments.note: The holding company and small remaining businesses. Revenue is minor here — but this is where most of the quarter's $3.0B of hedge mark-to-market gains landed.

takeaways.text: Mark-to-market gains on hedges that don't qualify for hedge accounting added $3.0B of pre-tax paper profit. Strip them out and adjusted EPS was $1.24, up about 10% — a good quarter, not a doubled one.
takeaways.title: Paper hedge gains did the doubling

takeaways.text: FPL earned $1,620M, up 11%, by investing about $2.4B in the quarter into Florida's grid and generation — regulated capital employed grew roughly 9%, and typical residential bills remain about 37% below the national average.
takeaways.title: Florida kept compounding

takeaways.text: Energy Resources added 3.7 GW of renewables and storage to its backlog (including 2.4 GW of batteries), taking it to about 36.7 GW — with big-load data-center projects emerging as a new growth lane.
takeaways.title: The backlog keeps growing

verdict: GAAP profit nearly doubled to $4.8B, but almost all of the jump was $3.0B of paper gains on hedges — the underlying utilities earned an adjusted $1.24 a share, up 10%.
